0: Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint by singNsong (Ize Press), with art by Sleepy-C, is a fantasy adventure about a reader who knows exactly how the world ends. Office worker Kim Dokja has spent years as the only reader of an obscure web novel. The day he finishes it, the story's apocalypse becomes real, and he's the only one who knows what happens next. It's a clever, tense read for fans of survival stories and stories about stories.
1: Villains Are Destined to Die by Gwon Gyeoeul and SUOL (Ize Press) is a romantic fantasy about surviving a game where every choice counts. A young woman wakes up inside a dating sim as Penelope Eckart, the villainess of its hardest mode, whose every route ends in her death. Affection meters float over the heads of the male leads, and one wrong word can be fatal. It's a sharp, stylish pick for fans of villainess and reincarnation stories.
2: The Misfit of Demon King Academy by Shu (Yen Press) is a fantasy action light novel about a legend nobody recognizes. Two thousand years after his death, the Demon King Anos Voldigoad is reborn and enrolls at an academy meant to find his successor. The school's tests can't measure his power, so they label him a misfit. Readers who enjoy an overpowered hero calmly flattening everyone who doubts him will have a great time here.
3: Kagurabachi by Takeru Hokazono (Viz Media) is a supernatural action story about a sword and a grudge. Chihiro Rokuhira grew up learning from his father, a master swordsmith who forged enchanted blades. When sorcerers murder his father and steal those swords, Chihiro takes up the last of his father's work and goes after them. It's a lean, stylish revenge story with striking sword fights, a good fit for readers who like their action cool and focused.
4: Monthly Girls' Nozaki-kun by Izumi Tsubaki (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy about a love confession that goes sideways. High schooler Chiyo Sakura finally tells her crush, Umetaro Nozaki, how she feels, and he hands her an autograph. It turns out the stoic Nozaki is a popular shojo manga artist, and soon Chiyo is helping out as his assistant. It's a gentle, very funny send-up of shojo manga that fans of the genre will especially enjoy.
5: The Devil is a Part-Timer by Satoshi Wagahara (Yen Press), with manga art by Akio Hiiragi, is a fantasy comedy about a demon lord stuck in a day job. Defeated in his own world, the Demon Lord Satan escapes through a portal and lands in modern Tokyo, nearly powerless. To pay rent, he takes a job at a fast-food restaurant and aims to work his way up. Then the hero who beat him follows him there. It's a warm, silly workplace comedy.
6: Oh My Goddess! by Kosuke Fujishima (Dark Horse) is a romantic comedy about one very lucky wrong number. Lonely college student Keiichi Morisato accidentally calls the Goddess Relief Office, and the goddess Belldandy appears to grant him a single wish. Half joking, he wishes she would stay with him forever, and the wish comes true. It's a sweet, long-running classic for readers who like gentle romance, everyday mischief, and a bit of magic.
7: Gigant by Hiroya Oku (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi drama about an unlikely friendship with enormous stakes. Rei Yokoyama is a high schooler who dreams of making movies, and he's a fan of the adult video actress Papico. When they meet, a strange device gives her the power to grow to giant size, just as disasters begin striking Tokyo. It's a mature, fast-paced story for readers who like big action mixed with romance.
11: The Masterful Cat Is Depressed Again Today by Hitsuji Yamada (Seven Seas) is a cozy comedy about a cat who runs the household. Office worker Saku Fukuzawa can barely keep her life together, but her cat Yukuko has it handled. Yukuko is huge, walks on two legs, and cooks, cleans, and shops better than any person could. It's a warm, funny slice-of-life read, perfect for cat lovers and anyone who wishes someone would take care of the chores.
12: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime by Fuse (Kodansha), with manga art by Taiki Kawakami, is a fantasy adventure about starting over as the weakest monster around. Satoru Mikami, an ordinary 37-year-old, is stabbed on a Tokyo street and wakes up in another world as a slime. After befriending a sealed storm dragon, he takes the name Rimuru and starts building something new. It's an upbeat, easygoing isekai about friendship and community.
13: The Case Files of Jeweler Richard by Mika Akatsuki (Seven Seas), based on the novels by Nanako Tsujimura, is a gentle mystery about gems and the people who love them. College student Seiji Nakata rescues an elegant foreign man from a group of drunks. The man is Richard, a jeweler, and Seiji soon takes a part-time job at his Ginza shop. Each customer arrives with a stone and a story, making this a quiet, thoughtful read.
14: Beastars by Paru Itagaki (Viz Media) is a psychological drama set at a school for animals, where carnivores and herbivores live side by side. Legoshi is a tall, quiet gray wolf at Cherryton Academy who tries hard not to frighten anyone. When an alpaca student is killed on campus, suspicion falls on the carnivores, and Legoshi starts to question his own instincts. It's a thoughtful, intense story for readers who like character-driven drama with real weight.
18: Cardcaptor Sakura by CLAMP (Kodansha) is a magical girl adventure about a book that should have stayed closed. Ten-year-old Sakura Kinomoto opens a strange book in her father's library and accidentally scatters the magical Clow Cards across town. Kero, the cards' little guardian, asks her to catch them all again. It's a sweet, beautifully drawn classic about friendship and courage, a great fit for younger readers and longtime fans alike.
19: Initial D by Shuichi Shigeno (Tokyopop) is a street racing drama about a driver who doesn't know how good he is. High schooler Takumi Fujiwara has spent years delivering tofu for his father's shop in an old Toyota AE86, racing down Mount Akina before dawn. When local racers learn who's behind the wheel of that car, Takumi gets pulled into the world of mountain pass racing. It's a classic for car fans and anyone who loves a good rivalry.
21: DanDaDan by Yukinobu Tatsu (Viz Media) is an action comedy about the supernatural, all of it. Momo Ayase believes in ghosts but not aliens, and her classmate Okarun believes in aliens but not ghosts. To settle it, each visits the other's haunted spot, and both turn out to be right. Soon they're caught up in a wild mix of spirits, UFOs, and growing feelings. It's fast, funny, and strange in the best way.
23: Pita-Ten by Koge-Donbo (Tokyopop) is a sweet comedy about a boy and the angel next door. Kotarou Higuchi is a serious, hardworking elementary schooler who keeps mostly to himself. Then Misha moves in next door, a cheerful, clumsy girl who happens to be an angel in training, and she decides to make him happy whether he likes it or not. It's a light, adorable read for fans of gentle romance and magical everyday comedy.
24: What's Wrong with Secretary Kim? by Jeong Gyeong-yun (Yen Press), with art by Kim Myeong-mi, is a romantic comedy set in a corporate office. Lee Young-joon is a brilliant, handsome, and spectacularly self-absorbed company vice chairman. For nine years, his secretary Kim Mi-so has kept his life running perfectly. Then she announces she's quitting, and he can't understand why. It's a fun, flirty office romance for fans of the K-drama.
25: Death March to the Parallel World Rhapsody by Ayamegumu (Yen Press), based on the novels by Hiro Ainana, is a fantasy adventure that starts with a nap. Exhausted programmer Ichiro Suzuki dozes off during a crunch and wakes in a world that looks like the games he builds. One emergency spell wipes out an army and leaves him wildly overleveled. Mostly, he just wants to sightsee, making this a relaxed, easygoing isekai.
28: Hunter x Hunter by Yoshihiro Togashi (Viz Media) is an action adventure about a boy searching for the father he never knew. Young Gon Freecss learns that his father, Ging, left home to become a Hunter, one of the elite adventurers who track treasure, monsters, and the unknown. Gon leaves his island to take the dangerous Hunter Exam and follow in his footsteps. It's an inventive, rewarding series for readers who love clever battles and deep worldbuilding.
30: Black Bird by Kanoko Sakurakouji (Viz Media) is a supernatural romance about a girl the demons won't leave alone. Misao Harada has always been able to see spirits, and lately they've grown dangerous. On her sixteenth birthday, her childhood friend Kyo returns and reveals that he's a tengu, a demon, and that her blood can grant great power to whoever claims her. It's a dark, dramatic romance for older shojo readers.
33: Food Wars! by Yuto Tsukuda (Viz Media), with art by Shun Saeki, is a cooking comedy about a kid from a diner taking on the elite. Soma Yukihira has grown up cooking at his father's small family restaurant. Then his father sends him to Totsuki Culinary Academy, a cutthroat school where only a handful of students graduate. It's a loud, funny, over-the-top series with real recipes and food reactions you won't forget.
35: Dragon Ball Z by Akira Toriyama (Viz Media) is an action adventure that picks up years after Goku's childhood journeys. Now grown and a father, Goku is living a peaceful life with his young son, Gohan. Then a powerful alien named Raditz arrives on Earth, claiming to be Goku's brother and revealing that Goku isn't from Earth at all. It's a classic of big battles and bigger power-ups, a cornerstone of shonen manga.
37: The Duke of Death and His Maid by Koharu Inoue (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about love you can't touch. As a child, the young duke was cursed so that any living thing he touches dies. Sent to live in a lonely mansion, he has only his butler and his maid, Alice, who loves to tease him and stand just out of reach. It's a sweet, gently gothic romance for readers who enjoy slow-burn love stories.
38: Mashle: Magic and Muscles by Hajime Komoto (Viz Media) is a fantasy comedy about a boy with no magic in a world built on it. Mash Burnedead was born without any magical ability, so he trained his body instead. To protect the quiet life he shares with his adoptive father, he enrolls at a prestigious magic academy and solves every problem with sheer strength. It's a goofy, deadpan action comedy, great for fans of One-Punch Man.
39: Fire Force by Atsushi Ohkubo (Kodansha) is a supernatural action series about firefighters who battle burning people. In a future Tokyo, ordinary people spontaneously combust and turn into monsters called Infernals. Shinra Kusakabe, a teen who can ignite his feet and fly, joins Special Fire Force Company 8 to fight them and become a hero. It's a stylish, high-energy action story for readers who like fast fights and a mystery underneath.
42: Daemons of the Shadow Realm by Hiromu Arakawa (Square Enix) is a fantasy action story from the creator of Fullmetal Alchemist. Yuru lives in a remote mountain village, hunting and caring for his twin sister, Asa, who is kept apart from everyone. When strangers attack the village, Yuru learns that much of what he believed about his home and his sister isn't true. It's an inventive, twisty adventure with Arakawa's trademark mix of humor and heart.
43: No Matter How I Look at It, It's You Guys' Fault I'm Not Popular! by Nico Tanigawa (Yen Press) is a comedy about a girl whose social life isn't going to plan. Tomoko Kuroki was sure high school would make her popular. Instead, she's painfully awkward, barely speaks to classmates, and overthinks everything. Her schemes to fix it go hilariously wrong. It's a cringe comedy for anyone who remembers feeling invisible at school.
45: As a Reincarnated Aristocrat, I'll Use My Appraisal Skill to Rise in the World by Miraijin A (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure about finding the right people. A man reborn as Ars Louvent, the son of a minor noble, discovers he can see anyone's hidden talents and potential at a glance. In a land on the edge of war, he uses that gift to recruit overlooked people. It's a strategic, good-natured isekai for readers who like kingdom-building stories.
46: Homunculus by Hideo Yamamoto (Seven Seas) is a psychological drama about seeing what people hide. Susumu Nakoshi is a former businessman living out of his car. A medical student offers him money to undergo trepanation, an experimental procedure that drills a small hole in his skull. Afterward, Nakoshi begins to see some people as strange, distorted figures that seem to reflect their inner selves. It's an unsettling, mature read for fans of psychological seinen.
47: Princess Resurrection by Yasunori Mitsunaga (Kodansha) is a horror action series about a boy brought back to serve a monster princess. Hiro Hiyorimi is killed in an accident on his way to visit his sister. A mysterious girl called Hime brings him back to life with her blood, binding him to her as a servant. Now he has to protect her from the monsters who want her crown. It's a darkly funny monster mash for fans of gothic action.
48: Yona of the Dawn by Mizuho Kusanagi (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure about a sheltered princess forced to grow up fast. Yona has spent her life pampered in the palace, in love with her cousin Su-won. On her sixteenth birthday, she witnesses something that shatters her world and has to flee with only her bodyguard, Hak, at her side. It's a moving, beautifully drawn story of courage and found family.
52: Re:Monster by Kanekiru Kogitsune (Seven Seas), with manga art by Haruyoshi Kobayakawa, is a fantasy action story about starting at the bottom of the food chain. After he's killed, a young man is reborn in another world as a goblin, one of the weakest monsters around. Luckily, he keeps his memories and gains new abilities from whatever he eats. It's a gritty, survival-minded isekai for readers who like watching a hero grow stronger step by step.
55: The Magical Revolution of the Reincarnated Princess and the Genius Young Lady by Piero Karasu (Yen Press) is a fantasy light novel with a sweet yuri romance at its heart. Princess Anisphia remembers a past life, can't use magic herself, and invents a science she calls magicology instead. When the duke's daughter Euphyllia is publicly dumped by her fiancé, Anis's own brother, Anis sweeps in to take her home. It's a warm, clever read.
56: How Heavy Are the Dumbbells You Lift? by Yabako Sandrovich (Seven Seas), with art by MAAM, is a gym comedy about getting fit and having fun. High schooler Hibiki Sakura loves to eat, and she decides it's time to lose some weight. At the gym, she runs into her classmate Akemi Soryuin, a sweet honor student who is secretly obsessed with muscles. It's a silly, upbeat comedy that sneaks in real workout tips along the way.
59: Fool Night by Kasumi Yasuda (Viz Media) is a sci-fi drama set in a world that hasn't seen the sun in over a century. With no sunlight, plants are precious, and people can sell themselves to be slowly transformed into trees that produce oxygen. Toshiro Ichiya is young, poor, and out of options, so he signs up. As the change begins, he starts hearing voices no one else can. It's a haunting, thoughtful read.
61: Kaiju No. 8 by Naoya Matsumoto (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action series about a man who becomes the monster he wanted to fight. Kafka Hibino is 32 and works cleaning up after kaiju attacks, long after giving up on joining the Defense Force. When a small kaiju gets inside him, he gains the power to turn into one himself. It's an exciting, big-hearted action story about chasing a dream when you think it's too late.
63: You and I Are Polar Opposites by Kocha Agasawa (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy about two people who couldn't be more different. Suzuki is a bubbly girl who works hard to fit in and say what others want to hear. Her classmate Tani is quiet, blunt, and doesn't care what anyone thinks of him. When she starts to fall for him, she has no idea how to reach someone so unlike her. It's a sweet, funny, very relatable read.
64: My Wife Has No Emotion by Jiro Sugiura (Seven Seas) is a gentle sci-fi romance about love and a household robot. Takuma is a lonely salaryman who buys a robot named Mina to help with the cooking and cleaning. Mina is efficient, literal, and has no emotions, or at least, she isn't supposed to. As Takuma gets attached to her, she begins to learn what being cared for means. It's a sweet, cozy read with a touch of melancholy.
65: Bakemonogatari by Oh! great (Vertical), adapting the novels by NisiOisin, is a supernatural romance full of strange spirits and sharp dialogue. Koyomi Araragi, a high schooler with a recent vampire problem, catches a classmate, Hitagi Senjougahara, when she falls down a staircase and discovers she weighs almost nothing. She's been touched by an oddity, and she isn't the only one. It's a stylish, witty series for readers who enjoy clever banter and eerie mysteries.
66: Haikyu!! by Haruichi Furudate (Viz Media) is a volleyball story about a short kid who dreams of flying. Shoyo Hinata fell in love with volleyball watching a small player soar on TV. In high school, he joins Karasuno's team, only to find his new teammate is Tobio Kageyama, the gifted setter who crushed him in his first match. It's an exciting, warm sports series about teamwork, rivalry, and getting better.
70: Reincarnated as a Sword by Yuu Tanaka (Seven Seas), with manga art by Tomowo Maruyama, is a fantasy adventure about a hero who is also a weapon. A man from Earth wakes up in another world as a talking magic sword, stuck in a monster-filled forest. He meets Fran, a young catgirl escaping slavery, and the two join forces as she sets out to become stronger. It's a warm, action-packed isekai built on a sweet partnership.
73: Overlord: The Undead King Oh! by Juami (Yen Press) is a comedy spinoff of the dark fantasy Overlord series by Kugane Maruyama. Ainz Ooal Gown, the skeletal sorcerer and ruler of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, is a gamer trapped in another world doing his best to look like a fearsome overlord. This chibi gag series plays up his everyday worries and his loyal, over-the-top servants. It's a light, silly treat for Overlord fans.
76: The Detective Is Already Dead by nigozyu (Yen Press) is a mystery adventure that begins after the story usually ends. Kimihiko Kimizuka is a magnet for trouble. Years ago, he met a brilliant detective named Siesta on a plane and spent three years as her assistant, solving cases around the world. Now she's gone, and he just wants a quiet life, but trouble finds him again. It's a twisty, bittersweet read for mystery fans.
77: Arpeggio of Blue Steel by Ark Performance (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi naval action series about a war for the oceans. A mysterious fleet of warships called the Fleet of Fog has driven humanity off the seas. Young captain Gunzo Chihaya commands the I-401, a Fog submarine whose human-shaped avatar, Iona, has chosen to fight alongside people. It's a tactical, exciting read for fans of naval battles and sci-fi strategy.
79: Yokohama Station SF by Yuba Isukari (Yen Press) is a sci-fi adventure set in a very strange future. Yokohama Station has grown on its own for centuries, slowly swallowing almost all of Japan. Hiroto lives on a coastal strip outside it, until he's handed a pass that lets him travel inside for five days. It's a quiet, imaginative journey for readers who enjoy offbeat worldbuilding and exploration stories.
81: Arifureta: From Commonplace to World's Strongest by Ryo Shirakome (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy action story about an underdog clawing his way back. Hajime Nagumo is summoned to another world with his whole class, but his only gift is a humble crafting skill. After a classmate betrays him, he falls into the depths of a deadly labyrinth and has to fight his way out alone. It's a good pick for readers who like gritty isekai with a fierce, self-made hero.
82: Overlord by Kugane Maruyama (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy told from the side of the villains. When the online game Yggdrasil shuts down for good, longtime player Momonga stays logged in to the very end. Instead of being kicked out, he wakes up as his skeletal sorcerer avatar in a strange new world, with his guild's loyal servants now alive around him. Fans of isekai with an overpowered, scheming lead will enjoy it.
83: I"s by Masakazu Katsura (Viz Media) is a high school romance with a lot of heart. Ichitaka Seto has a huge crush on his classmate Iori Yoshizuki, a sweet girl who is starting to make a name for herself as a model and actress. He just can't seem to tell her how he feels, and things get more complicated when his childhood friend Itsuki comes back into his life. It's a warm, classic pick for fans of slow-burn teen love stories.
84: Love at Fourteen by Fuka Mizutani (Yen Press) is a gentle slice-of-life romance. Kanata and Kazuki are fourteen-year-old classmates who seem calm and grown-up next to everyone else in class. In secret, they are falling for each other, sneaking quiet moments together while trying to figure out what their feelings mean. It's soft, sweet, and quietly observant, perfect for readers who like innocent first-love stories with lovely art.
85: Banished From The Hero's Party by Zappon (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy romance light novel. Red was a skilled member of the hero's party until he was told he was no longer needed and sent away. Instead of seeking revenge, he heads to a quiet frontier town to open an apothecary, and his slow new life gets a lot sweeter when an old friend shows up wanting to work with him. It's a relaxing read for fans of low-stress fantasy.
86: Ai Ore! by Mayu Shinjo (Viz Media) is a gender-flipped shojo romance with a rock and roll edge. Akira is a pretty, delicate-looking guitarist at an all-boys school who is tired of being mistaken for a girl, while Mizuki is the tall, boyish "prince" of a nearby all-girls school. When the two meet, sparks fly and ideas about who should act like what get turned upside down. Readers who like bold, dramatic romance will have fun with it.
87: We Never Learn by Taishi Tsutsui (Viz Media) is a school romantic comedy about studying and crushes. Nariyuki Yuiga's family is struggling, and to earn the scholarship he needs for college, he has to tutor two genius classmates in the one subject each is terrible at. As more girls join his study sessions, his days get busier and his heart gets more confused. It's a light, funny harem comedy with a lot of warmth.
88: Kaguya-sama: Love Is War by Aka Akasaka (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy about pride getting in the way of love. Kaguya Shinomiya and Miyuki Shirogane run an elite academy's student council and clearly like each other, but both believe whoever confesses first loses. So every day turns into a battle of clever schemes to make the other one crack. It's sharp, silly, and a favorite among rom-com fans.
90: Gleipnir by Sun Takeda (Kodansha) is a dark supernatural action story with a strange twist. Shuichi Kagaya is an ordinary high schooler with a secret: he can transform into a giant, dog-like creature with a zipper on its back. When he saves his classmate Claire from a burning building, she discovers what he is, climbs inside him, and pulls them both into a dangerous fight among other people with powers. It's for readers who like intense, mature thrillers.
91: Daytime Shooting Star by Mika Yamamori (Viz Media) is a heartfelt shojo romance. Suzume is a country girl who moves to Tokyo to live with her uncle, and on her first day in the city she gets lost and is helped by a kind, offbeat stranger. He turns out to be her new homeroom teacher, and as she finds her place at school, her feelings grow complicated. It's a sweet, emotional read for fans of coming-of-age love stories.
93: Yurara by Chika Shiomi (Viz Media) is a supernatural shojo romance. Yurara is a shy high school girl who can see ghosts, and she has always kept that a secret, along with the bold, fierce guardian spirit inside her who comes out when she is in danger. When she meets classmates who also deal with spirits, she finds herself pulled into helping lost souls. It's a gentle mix of ghost stories and romance for shojo fans.
94: Konosuba: An Explosion on This Wonderful World! by Natsume Akatsuki (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy spinoff of Konosuba. Before she ever met Kazuma, Megumin was a young student in the Crimson Demon village with her heart set on explosion magic, the one flashy spell everyone says is useless. Along with her lonely rival Yunyun, she gets into all kinds of trouble on the way to becoming an archwizard. It's a fun read for Megumin fans and anyone who likes lighthearted fantasy.
95: King of Hell by Ra In-Soo and Kim Jae-Hwan (Tokyopop) is a Korean action fantasy with plenty of sword fights. Majeh was a legendary swordsman in life, and now he works for the King of Hell. Evil spirits have escaped from the underworld into the world of the living, and Majeh is sent back in a younger body to hunt them down. It's a fast, funny, and stylish adventure for readers who like martial arts and supernatural battles.
96: Baccano! by Ryohgo Narita (Yen Press) is a lively crime and fantasy light novel series set in Prohibition-era America. In 1930s New York, a mysterious elixir of immortality slips into the hands of gangsters, alchemists, and a pair of cheerful, clueless thieves, and their stories crash into one another. Told from many points of view, it's a fun read for anyone who likes big casts and twisty, stylish storytelling.
97: Orphen by Yoshinobu Akita (ADV) is a fantasy adventure about a sorcerer with a past. Orphen trained at the elite Tower of Fangs, but he walked away after a magical experiment turned someone he loved into a dragon. Now he wanders the land as a sharp-tongued sorcerer for hire, searching for a way to save her. It's a classic sword-and-sorcery story for readers who like magic, banter, and a hero on a personal quest.
98: Berserk by Kentaro Miura (Dark Horse) is a dark fantasy known for its brutal battles and detailed art. Guts, called the Black Swordsman, travels a grim medieval world carrying a sword almost too big to lift. He bears a cursed brand that draws demons to him at night, and he is hunting the creatures responsible for it. This is a mature, intense series best suited to adult readers who like heavy, sweeping fantasy.
99: AOI House by Adam Arnold and Shiei (Seven Seas) is a comedy about anime fans and the college life they share. Alex and Sandy are two guys who need a place to live, fast, and the only one they can find is a house full of girls who are huge anime fans with some very specific interests. Hijinks follow as everyone tries to get along under one roof. It's a goofy, affectionate send-up of fandom culture.
100: Helck by Nanao Nanaki (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure with a big heart and a sense of humor. The Demon King has died, and one of the contestants in the tournament to pick a new ruler is Helck, a cheerful human hero who says he wants to wipe out humanity. The demon official Vermilio is suspicious of him and sets out to uncover his real story. It's a funny, surprising pick for fantasy fans.
102: Bocchi the Rock! by Aki Hamaji (Yen Press) is a comedy about music, friendship, and social anxiety. Hitori Gotoh is a painfully shy high school girl who has practiced guitar for years, hoping to make friends by joining a band, but she has never worked up the courage to talk to anyone. Then an upbeat drummer named Nijika drags her into her band. It's funny, relatable, and great for anyone who loves music or has ever felt awkward.
103: Is This a Zombie? by Shinichi Kimura and Sacchi (Yen Press) is a supernatural action comedy. Ayumu Aikawa is a high school boy who was killed and brought back as a zombie by a quiet necromancer girl, and things get even stranger when he ends up with the powers of a magical girl, frilly outfit and all. It's a silly, over-the-top comedy for readers who like absurd humor and supernatural action.
105: Dead Mount Death Play by Ryohgo Narita and Shinta Fujimoto (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy thriller. The Corpse God, a feared necromancer, is finally defeated by a hero, but in that moment he is pulled into another body. He wakes up in modern-day Shinjuku as Shinobu Sotoba, a young boy who has just been murdered, and has to survive a city full of strange people with secrets of their own. It's a twisty, offbeat story for fans of urban fantasy.
107: The Wallflower by Tomoko Hayakawa (Kodansha) is a horror comedy with a big heart. Sunako Nakahara is a gloomy girl who loves horror movies, skeletons, and dark rooms. Her aunt makes a deal with four handsome young men that they can live in her mansion rent-free if they turn Sunako into a proper lady, and since Sunako has no interest at all, the chaos begins. It's a funny, quirky read for fans of comedy shojo.
108: Bloody Kiss by Kazuko Furumiya (Tokyopop) is a short vampire romance comedy. High school girl Kiyo inherits her grandmother's old house and plans to sell it to pay for her tuition. When she goes to check it out, she finds two vampires already living there, and they have no plans to leave. It's a quick, light read for fans of supernatural shojo romance.
109: A Terrified Teacher at Ghoul School by Mai Tanaka (Yen Press) is a supernatural comedy set in a school for yokai. A new teacher who is scared of anything spooky is assigned to a class full of monster students. She is easily frightened, but she cares about her kids and tries her best to teach them. It's a light, sweet comedy for readers who like cute yokai and school stories.
110: Lament of the Lamb by Kei Toume (Tokyopop) is a quiet, haunting drama with a touch of horror. Kazuna Takashiro is a high school boy who has started having strange cravings and frightening visions. He learns that his family carries an inherited illness that leaves its victims thirsting for blood, a truth that draws him back toward the half-sister he barely knew. It's moody and melancholy, best for readers who like slow, atmospheric stories.
111: Parallel Paradise by Lynn Okamoto (Seven Seas) is a fantasy story with heavy fanservice, best suited to adult readers. High school track star Youta Tada falls into a mysterious fantasy world. He soon discovers that he is the only man in this world, which is full of women living under a dark curse. It's a mature, steamy read for fans of ecchi isekai with a mystery at its core.
112: Ceres: Celestial Legend by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy romance. On their sixteenth birthday, Aya Mikage and her twin brother Aki are brought before their wealthy family for a strange test. Aya learns she carries the spirit of Ceres, a celestial maiden from legend, and her own family now wants her dead. It's a dramatic, emotional story for readers who like fantasy shojo with a darker edge.
113: Syrup: A Yuri Anthology (Seven Seas) is a collection of girls' love short stories by various creators. Each volume gathers a mix of romances between women, from sweet first crushes to grown-up relationships. Some stories are funny, some are tender, and some are bittersweet. It's a nice pick for readers who want to sample many yuri creators in one place.
114: World Trigger by Daisuke Ashihara (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action series about defending a city from invaders. Monsters called Neighbors pour through gates from another world, and the agency Border fights them off. Osamu Mikumo is a low-ranked Border trainee who meets Yuma Kuga, a new transfer student who turns out to be a Neighbor himself. It's a clever, strategic action story for readers who like team battles and tactics.
115: My Next Life as a Villainess: All Routes Lead to Doom! by Satoru Yamaguchi and Nami Hidaka (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Young noble Catarina Claes bumps her head and remembers her past life as a Japanese teen who loved otome games, then realizes she is now the villainess of one, with every ending leading to exile or death. Her earnest attempts to dodge her fate have very funny results. It's a cheerful pick for fans of villainess stories.
116: Sleepy Princess in the Demon Castle by Kagiji Kumanomata (Viz Media) is a fantasy comedy. Princess Syalis has been kidnapped by the Demon King and locked in his castle, but instead of waiting to be rescued, she has just one goal: getting a good night's sleep. She will happily raid the castle and outsmart demons for a better pillow. It's a cute, silly read for anyone who loves a nap.
118: 2.5 Dimensional Seduction by Yu Hashimoto (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about cosplay. Masamune Okumura is the only boy in his school's manga club, and he only has eyes for Liliel, a 2D character from his favorite series. Then a new classmate, Lilysa Amano, shows up wanting to cosplay as Liliel, and before long he is behind the camera. It's a fun pick for fans of fandom stories and rom-coms.
119: Attack on Titan: Before the Fall by Ryo Suzukaze and Satoshi Shiki (Kodansha) is an action prequel set long before the original Attack on Titan. Kuklo was born from a woman swallowed by a Titan, and people call him the Titan's Son. Treated as a curse and kept like an animal, he grows up determined to understand and fight the creatures that took everything from him. It's a good pick for fans who want more of the world of Attack on Titan.
120: Tales of Wedding Rings by Maybe (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance adventure. Sato's childhood friend Hime turns out to be a princess from another world, and when he follows her home, their wedding makes him the Ring King. To save her world from a dark threat, he must find and win over princesses from other lands. It's a fun, romantic adventure for fans of fantasy harem stories.
121: Muhyo and Roji's Bureau of Supernatural Investigation by Yoshiyuki Nishi (Viz Media) is a supernatural mystery series. Muhyo is a young genius executor, a kind of magic lawyer who judges and punishes evil spirits, and his kind, nervous assistant Roji is far less skilled but learning fast. Together they run a small office that takes on ghost cases of all kinds. It's a spooky, fun pick for readers who like supernatural mysteries.
122: Aoharu x Machinegun by Naoe (Yen Press) is an action comedy about the world of survival games. Hotaru Tachibana is a strong-willed high school student who is often mistaken for a boy, and after a run-in with a charming host, Hotaru ends up joining his airsoft team. Soon Hotaru is training for battles with toy guns and finding friendship along the way. It's a lively, funny read for fans of action and offbeat sports stories.
123: Happiness by Shuzo Oshimi (Kodansha) is a dark horror drama about a boy changed forever. Makoto Okazaki is a quiet high schooler who often gets picked on, until one night a mysterious girl attacks him in an alley and bites his neck. Afterward, his body starts changing, and he feels a new, terrible hunger. It's a moody, unsettling vampire story best for older readers who like psychological horror.
124: A Silent Voice by Yoshitoki Oima (Kodansha) is a moving drama about regret and second chances. In elementary school, Shoya Ishida bullied Shoko Nishimiya, a deaf transfer student, until she left the school. Years later, Shoya is lonely and full of guilt, and he decides to find Shoko and make things right. It's a tender, honest story about kindness and forgiveness that stays with you.
125: Choujin X by Sui Ishida (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action story. In a world where some people transform into superhumans called choujin, Tokio Kurohara is an anxious teenager who feels he doesn't measure up, until a terrible attack turns him into a choujin himself. Now he has to figure out what kind of person, and what kind of hero, he wants to be. It's a stylish, strange action series for readers who like dark superhero stories.
126: Akame ga Kill! by Takahiro and Tetsuya Tashiro (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy action series. Tatsumi is a country boy who travels to the capital hoping to earn money for his poor village, only to find the city rotten to the core. He joins Night Raid, a group of assassins fighting the corrupt government. It's a violent, intense action story for older readers who like high stakes and powerful weapons.
129: Arata: The Legend by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure. In another world, Arata of the Hime clan is forced to dress as a princess and is framed for a crime, while in modern Japan, high schooler Arata Hinohara is betrayed by his best friend. The two boys switch places, and Hinohara finds himself holding a legendary sword. It's a classic, sweeping quest story for fans of shonen fantasy.
131: Life Lessons with Uramichi Oniisan by Gaku Kuze (Kodansha) is a dry comedy about adulthood. Uramichi Omota is the cheerful gymnastics instructor on a children's TV show. Off camera, he is tired, gloomy, and fed up with grown-up life, and his dark thoughts tend to slip out during the show. It's a funny, relatable read for any adult who has ever had to smile through a long day.
133: Arifureta Zero by Ryo Shirakome (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action prequel to Arifureta: From Commonplace to World's Strongest. Thousands of years before Hajime's story, the world lives under gods who demand blind faith, and a spirited young girl named Miledi Reisen dreams of changing that. Together with others who share her goal, she sets out to fight back. It's a good pick for fans who want the history behind Arifureta.
134: Obey Me! The Comic by Subaru Nitou (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy based on the popular mobile game. An ordinary human is picked to study abroad in the Devildom, the world of demons, and is placed in the care of seven demon brothers, each a little dangerous and each with his own personality. It's a fun read for fans of the game and anyone who likes a handsome, chaotic cast.
135: Colette Decides to Die by Alto Yukimura (Viz Media) is a gentle fantasy romance. Colette is a young apothecary so overworked that she decides to end it all, but instead she ends up in the underworld, face to face with Hades. He asks her to treat his aches and pains, and she begins making regular visits. It's warm and cozy, for readers who like slow, healing romance.
139: Carole & Tuesday by Morito Yamataka (Yen Press) is a sci-fi music drama based on the anime. On a future Mars where most music is made by AI, Carole is a refugee working odd jobs in the big city, and Tuesday is a rich girl who has run away from home. When they meet by chance, they discover they make beautiful music together and decide to form a duo. It's a sweet, hopeful story for music lovers.
140: His Favorite by Suzuki Tanaka (Sublime) is a lighthearted boys' love romance. Yoshida is a plain, unremarkable high school boy who gets picked on by the girls in his class, while Sato, the school's handsome, popular guy, only has eyes for Yoshida. Their back-and-forth is full of teasing and slow-building feelings. It's a funny, sweet read for fans of school BL romances.
141: Sailor Moon by Naoko Takeuchi (Mixx) is a classic magical girl fantasy. Usagi Tsukino is a clumsy, crybaby schoolgirl until a talking black cat named Luna gives her the power to become Sailor Moon, a warrior who fights for love and justice. Soon she is gathering other Sailor Guardians and searching for the lost moon princess. It's the series that defined a generation of shojo fans.
142: Hakumei & Mikochi by Takuto Kashiki (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy slice-of-life story. Hakumei and Mikochi are two tiny women, only a few inches tall, who share a home in a tree hollow; one is energetic and handy, the other calm and a great cook. They share small adventures and everyday moments with the animals and little folk around them. It's peaceful and gorgeous, perfect for readers who love gentle stories.
145: Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid: Elma's Office Lady Diary by coolkyousinnjya and Ayami Kazama (Seven Seas) is a comedy spinoff of Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid. Elma is a dragon who came to Earth to bring Tohru home and ended up staying. Now she works at the same office as Kobayashi, learning how human jobs work and falling in love with human snacks. It's a light, funny read for fans of the original series.
146: No Game No Life by Yuu Kamiya (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure about gaming. Sora and Shiro are a brother and sister who are unbeatable gamers but rarely leave their room, until they are pulled into Disboard, a world where everything is decided by games. The two set their sights on beating the god of that world. It's a bright, clever read for fans of isekai and mind games.
147: Skip Beat by Yoshiki Nakamura (Viz Media) is a showbiz romantic comedy. Kyoko Mogami has given everything to support her childhood friend Sho as he becomes a pop star, until she overhears him calling her nothing more than a maid. Furious, she vows revenge by becoming a bigger star than he is. It's a funny, fiery story for readers who like strong heroines and slow-burn romance.
150: Nights with a Cat by Kyuryu Z (Yen Press) is a short, sweet comedy about life with a cat. A young office worker comes home each night to his cat, Fuku-chan. The stories capture the funny, silly, and affectionate moments of living with a feline, from naps and snacks to the cat's odd habits. It's a cozy pick for cat lovers.
151: Levius/est by Haruhisa Nakata (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action series and a continuation of Levius. In a steam-powered world, fighters with mechanical limbs battle in the brutal sport of Mechanical Martial Arts. Young fighter Levius continues his rise through the ranks, while his past and the people around him draw him into darker conflicts. It's a stylish, detailed story for fans of fighting and steampunk.
153: Otaku Elf by Akihiko Higuchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Elda is an elf who has lived at Takamimi Shrine in Tokyo for centuries, and these days she is a shut-in otaku who spends her time playing games and collecting merchandise. Koito, the shrine maiden assigned to look after her, gets pulled into her lazy, nerdy world. It's a lighthearted, funny read for fans of geeky comedy.
154: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- by Tappei Nagatsuki (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy light novel. Subaru Natsuki is an ordinary guy who suddenly finds himself in a fantasy world with one strange power: when he dies, he goes back in time to an earlier point. With every loop, he fights to save the people he cares about. It's a tense, emotional story for readers who like psychological fantasy.
158: Chained Soldier by Takahiro and Yohei Takemura (Yen Press) is an action fantasy with heavy fanservice, best suited to adult readers. Yuuki Wakura is a high school boy who stumbles into the Mato, a dangerous realm filled with monsters, and is saved by Kyouka Uzen, commander of an all-female anti-demon force. Her power turns him into a mighty fighter, but it comes at a price. It's a mature, action-heavy read.
160: I Want to End This Love Game by Yuki Domoto (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy about two childhood friends. Since they were kids, they've played a game in which each tries to make the other blush by saying "I love you," and now that they're in high school, it's getting harder to win. Both are hiding real feelings behind the teasing. It's a sweet, silly rom-com for fans of slow-burn romance.
161: X/1999 by CLAMP (Viz Media) is a dark apocalyptic fantasy. Kamui Shiro, a young man with powerful psychic abilities, returns to Tokyo after years away as the fate of the world draws near. Two groups of supernatural fighters want him on their side, and his return brings him back to the childhood friends he left behind. It's an intense, dramatic story for fans of CLAMP and dark fantasy.
163: Millennium Snow by Bisco Hatori (Viz Media) is a gentle supernatural romance. Chiyuki is a cheerful girl with a weak heart who has been told she may not live to see another winter. Then she meets Toya, a gruff young vampire who refuses to drink human blood, and she decides to change his mind about life, and her own. It's a sweet, bittersweet read for fans of Ouran's creator and soft paranormal romance.
164: Delicious in Dungeon by Ryoko Kui (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure with a cooking twist. When a red dragon swallows his sister Falin deep in a dungeon, the knight Laios rushes back in to save her, with no money and almost no supplies. His solution is to eat the monsters along the way. It's funny, clever, and packed with loving detail, perfect for fantasy fans and food lovers alike.
165: Though I Am an Inept Villainess by Satsuki Nakamura (Seven Seas) is a palace comedy set in a Chinese-inspired imperial court. Kou Reirin is the most beloved maiden competing to become the next empress, until her bitter rival Shu Keigetsu swaps their bodies. Stuck in the body of the court's most hated woman, Reirin turns out to be far tougher than anyone expected. It's a fun, upbeat story about two very different women.
166: Death Note by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a psychological thriller about power and justice. Brilliant student Light Yagami finds a notebook dropped by the death god Ryuk: write a name in it, and that person dies. Light sets out to rid the world of criminals, until a mysterious detective known only as L starts closing in. It's a tense battle of wits that keeps you turning pages.
167: Blue Period by Tsubasa Yamaguchi (Kodansha) is a coming-of-age drama about discovering art. Yatora Yaguchi is a popular high schooler with good grades who feels oddly empty inside. When a painting moves him for the first time, he throws himself into art and sets his sights on one of Japan's toughest art schools. It's honest and inspiring, especially for anyone who has ever fallen hard for a creative passion.
168: Rooster Fighter by Shu Sakuratani (Viz Media) is an action comedy that's exactly as wild as it sounds. Keiji is a rooster, a regular barnyard bird, who wanders the land battling giant demons that attack humans. He's tough, honorable, and very serious about his mission, even as everyone around him sees just a chicken. It's ridiculous in the best way, with surprisingly heartfelt moments and big, dramatic fights.
169: One Week Friends by Matcha Hazuki (Yen Press) is a gentle romance about friendship and memory. Yuki Hase wants to befriend his quiet classmate Kaori Fujimiya, but she keeps everyone at a distance. He learns why: every Monday, her memories of her friends reset. Yuki decides to become her friend again, week after week. It's a tender, quiet story for readers who enjoy soft, emotional school romances.
170: Marriage Toxin by Joumyaku and Mizuki Yoda (Viz Media) is an action romantic comedy. Hikaru Gero is a deadly assassin from a clan of poison users, but he's hopeless with women, and his family needs him to marry. Help comes from Mei Kinosaki, a professional marriage swindler, who teaches him how to date while assassins come after him. It's a fun mix of stylish fights and dating chaos.
173: Dimension W by Yuji Iwahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action series set in a near future powered by coils, devices that draw energy from a hidden fourth dimension. Kyoma Mabuchi is a collector who hunts illegal coils and refuses to use them himself. His world changes when he meets Mira, a surprisingly human android girl. It's a stylish, mystery-driven series for fans of gritty sci-fi and odd-couple partnerships.
174: Yu-Gi-Oh! Zexal by Shin Yoshida and Naoto Miyashi (Viz Media) is a card-battle adventure in the Yu-Gi-Oh! universe. Yuma Tsukumo is an energetic kid who dreams of becoming a dueling champion, even though he keeps losing. Everything changes when he meets Astral, a mysterious spirit who has lost his memories, scattered across powerful Number cards. It's fast, bright, and full of duels, great for younger fans of the franchise.
175: Insomniacs After School by Makoto Ojiro (Viz Media) is a quiet romance about two sleepless teens. Ganta Nakami can't sleep at night and is exhausted and prickly at school. Then he finds classmate Isaki Magari napping in the school's abandoned observatory, and learns she has insomnia too. Together they revive the astronomy club to keep their secret hideout. It's calm, warm, and beautifully drawn, perfect for a late-night read.
176: Yu Yu Hakusho by Yoshihiro Togashi (Viz Media) is a supernatural action series. Yusuke Urameshi is a tough delinquent who dies saving a little kid from a car, surprising even the afterlife. Given a chance to return, he becomes a Spirit Detective, investigating demons and spirits in the human world. It grows from ghostly cases into big tournament battles, a classic for fans of action-packed shonen.
177: Pandora Hearts by Jun Mochizuki (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy mystery. Oz Vessalius is the cheerful heir of a noble family, but during his coming-of-age ceremony he is accused of a sin he doesn't understand and thrown into the Abyss. There he meets Alice, a fierce girl with no memory of who she is. It's lavish and gothic, with a twisting mystery for readers who like puzzles.
180: The Daily Lives of High School Boys by Yasunobu Yamauchi (Vertical) is a sketch comedy about the ordinary silliness of teenage boys. Tadakuni, Hidenori, and Yoshitake attend an all-boys school, where they turn boring days into elaborate role-play, dramatic misunderstandings, and terrible schemes. There's no big plot, just one hilarious situation after another. It's a great pick for readers who love deadpan, absurd humor.
181: The Dark History of the Reincarnated Villainess by Akiharu Touka (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Konoha is reborn into the world of the story she wrote as a teenager, filled with all the over-the-top ideas she'd rather forget, and she's the villainess. Now she has to avoid her doomed ending while facing her most embarrassing creations. It's a fun, cringe-filled ride for fans of villainess stories.
184: Yu-Gi-Oh! by Kazuki Takahashi (Viz Media) is the adventure that started the card-game craze. Shy high schooler Yugi Mutou solves the ancient Millennium Puzzle, awakening a bold spirit who shares his body. Together they face dangerous games, and later card duels, against rivals like Seto Kaiba. It's darker and stranger than the anime, and fun for longtime fans who want to see where it all began.
185: Living-Room Matsunaga-san by Keiko Iwashita (Kodansha) is a warm romance set in a share house. High schooler Meeko moves into her uncle's house full of adult tenants, where she meets Matsunaga, a grumpy-looking man who turns out to be kind. As she spends time with him in the shared living room, she starts to fall for him. It's sweet, cozy, and full of everyday moments.
186: Voice Over! Seiyu Academy by Maki Minami (Viz Media) is a comedy about chasing a dream career. Hime Kino dreams of becoming a voice actress like her idol, but her husky voice wasn't what anyone expected. She enrolls in the voice acting program at Holly Academy and lands in a class full of oddballs. It's bubbly, funny, and fun for anime fans curious about voice acting.
187: My Senpai Is Annoying by Shiromanta (Seven Seas) is an office romantic comedy. Futaba Igarashi is a small, hardworking employee whose senior coworker, Takeda, is huge, loud, and always teasing her. He's also kind and always looks out for her, and Futaba's feelings start to change. It's a light, sweet workplace story for anyone who enjoys gentle romance with lots of laughs.
189: Sweetness and Lightning by Gido Amagakure (Kodansha) is a slice-of-life story about family and food. Kohei Inuzuka is a widowed teacher raising his young daughter, Tsumugi, but he doesn't know how to cook. When his student Kotori offers her family's restaurant kitchen, the three begin making home-cooked meals together. It's heartwarming and comforting, with real recipes along the way.
190: My Heavenly Hockey Club by Ai Morinaga (Del Rey) is a goofy sports comedy. Hana Suzuki only cares about eating and sleeping, but handsome Izumi Oda wants her on the school's all-boys hockey club. Lured by the promise of trips and good food, she agrees, and finds herself surrounded by a team of eccentric boys. It's silly, upbeat fun for fans of reverse-harem comedies. The English release stopped before the series finished.
191: Masamune-kun's Revenge by Hazuki Takeoka and Tiv (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about payback. As a chubby kid, Masamune Makabe was cruelly rejected by the rich girl Aki Adagaki. Years later he returns to her school slim and handsome, with a plan to make her fall for him and then dump her. It's a fun, scheming romance full of twists. The English release stopped before the series finished.
192: Naruto: Chibi Sasuke's Sharingan Legend by Kenji Taira (Viz Media) is a gag spin-off of Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto. Pint-sized Sasuke sets out on his quest to restore his clan, but nothing goes as planned with his oddball teammates in tow. Big dramatic moments from the original become ridiculous here. It's a light, goofy read for Naruto fans who want to see the characters in a sillier light.
193: Assassination Classroom by Yusei Matsui (Viz Media) is an action comedy with a big heart. A tentacled creature has blown up most of the moon and threatens to destroy Earth next, but first he wants to teach a class of misfit students. Class 3-E's assignment is to kill their new teacher before graduation. It's funny, clever, and surprisingly moving, with a teacher you'll grow to love.
194: Kaina of the Great Snow Sea by Tsutomu Nihei (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure set in a frozen world. Kaina lives high on the canopy of enormous trees, among a dwindling people who rarely meet outsiders. His life changes when a princess named Liliha arrives from far below, searching for a way to save her land. It's atmospheric and quietly beautiful, a great entry point to Nihei's vast worlds.
195: The Misfit of Demon King Academy by Shu (Square Enix) is a fantasy action series. Anos Voldigoad, the most powerful demon king in history, reincarnates two thousand years in the future. He enrolls at the academy meant to find his successor, only to be labeled a misfit by its flawed tests. Overwhelming power meets an unimpressed school. It's fun for fans of confident, overpowered heroes.
196: Kakegurui Twin by Homura Kawamoto (Yen Press) is a prequel to Kakegurui, a psychological thriller about high-stakes gambling. Mary Saotome transfers to Hyakkaou Private Academy, where student rank is determined by gambling. She quickly learns how cutthroat the school is, and starts building her own crew to fight back. It's tense, stylish, and a fun look at a fan-favorite character before the main series.
197: Magilumiere Magical Girls Inc. by Sekka Iwata (Viz Media) is a workplace comedy with magic. Kana Sakuragi is a struggling job hunter who gets hired by a small startup where magical girls are professionals paid to fight monsters. With a lot to learn and a dedicated team behind her, Kana throws herself into the job. It's cheerful and clever, perfect for anyone who has ever started a new job.
198: Hellsing by Kouta Hirano (Dark Horse) is a gothic action horror series. The Hellsing Organization protects Britain from vampires and ghouls, and its greatest weapon is Alucard, an ancient and terrifyingly powerful vampire. When a young police officer named Seras Victoria is caught in an attack, Alucard turns her, and she joins the fight. It's violent, stylish, and over the top, for readers who love bloody, dark action.
199: Nightmare Inspector: Yumekui Kenbun by Shin Mashiba (Viz Media) is a supernatural mystery anthology. In a teahouse in Taisho-era Tokyo, a mysterious baku named Hiruko eats people's nightmares, as long as they can tell him what the dream is about. Each visitor brings a new dream, and a new secret. It's eerie, beautiful, and haunting, perfect for fans of short, strange tales.
200: Dance in the Vampire Bund by Nozomu Tamaki (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action series. Mina Tepes, the young-looking queen of the vampires, reveals her kind to the world and creates a special district off Tokyo's coast for vampires. Her loyal guardian, Akira, must protect her from enemies everywhere. It's dark and political, with lots of action, for fans of vampire stories with mature themes.
202: Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid: Kanna's Daily Life by coolkyousinnjya (Seven Seas) is a slice-of-life spin-off. Kanna Kamui is a little dragon girl living in the human world, going to elementary school and making friends. Her days are filled with small adventures and silly misunderstandings. It's sweet, calm, and charming, a great pick for fans of the main series or anyone looking for something cozy.
203: Real Account by Okushou (Kodansha) is a psychological thriller about social media. Ataru Kashiwagi is pulled into a deadly game inside a social networking app, along with thousands of other users. The rules are simple: lose all your followers, and you die, along with everyone who follows you. It's a dark, twisty survival story for fans of death games and online drama.
204: Berserk of Gluttony by Isshiki Ichika (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action series. Fate Graphite is a lowly gatekeeper mocked for his useless skill, Gluttony, which only makes him hungry. When he kills a thief, he discovers the truth: Gluttony lets him devour the power of everyone he defeats. It's dark and action-packed, fun for fans of underdog heroes who grow stronger.
205: The Honor Student at Magic High School by Tsutomu Satou (Yen Press) is a spin-off of The Irregular at Magic High School. Miyuki Shiba is the top student at a magic school, while her brother Tatsuya is stuck in the lower class. This series follows Miyuki and her friends through school life and adventures. It's lighter than the main series and fun for fans who want to see Miyuki's side.
207: Silent Möbius by Kia Asamiya (Udon) is a sci-fi action series set in a futuristic Tokyo. Demons called Lucifer Hawks are slipping through to our world, and the only ones who can stop them are the women of AMP, a police unit trained in magic and technology. Katsumi Liqueur joins the team and must discover her own powers. It's a classic for fans of cyberpunk.
208: World's End Harem by LINK and Kotaro Shono (Seven Seas) is a mature sci-fi series. Reito Mizuhara wakes up after years in cryosleep to find that a virus has killed almost every man on Earth. Now he's one of the few left, and the women in charge want him to help repopulate the world. It's provocative and explicit, for adult readers who enjoy ecchi with a mystery behind it.
209: If It's for My Daughter, I'd Even Defeat a Demon Lord by CHIROLU (Seven Seas) is a warm fantasy slice-of-life. Dale is a skilled young adventurer who finds a little demon girl, Latina, alone in the forest. He takes her home and becomes her father, and his whole life changes. It's sweet and heartwarming, a gentle story for fans of found family and cozy fantasy.
210: Blade of the Immortal by Hiroaki Samura (Dark Horse) is a historical action series. Manji is a samurai cursed with immortality: his wounds heal no matter how badly he's hurt. To lift the curse, he must kill a thousand evil men. When a young girl named Rin asks for his help getting revenge for her parents, he agrees. It's brutal and beautifully drawn, a classic of samurai manga.
211: Spy Classroom by Takemachi (Yen Press) is a spy action light novel. Klaus is a brilliant spy who's asked to train a team of girls who failed out of spy academy for an impossible mission. The only problem is that he's terrible at teaching. The girls must come up with their own way to catch up. It's clever and full of twists, for fans of spy games.
213: An Incurable Case of Love by Maki Enjoji (Viz Media) is a romance set in a hospital. Nanase Sakura became a nurse after meeting a kind doctor who once helped her. When she meets him again at work, he turns out to be the hospital's cold and demanding Dr. Tendo. It's a mature, sweet romance for readers who like workplace stories and grumpy love interests.
215: Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction by Inio Asano (Viz Media) is a sci-fi slice-of-life story. Years after a giant alien mothership appeared over Tokyo, life goes on almost normally. High school friends Kadode and Ouran go to school, play video games, and worry about exams, all under a hovering threat. It's funny, strange, and thoughtful, for readers who like stories with layers.
217: The Apothecary Diaries by Natsu Hyuuga (Square Enix) is a historical mystery light novel. Maomao is a young apothecary who is kidnapped and sold as a servant to the imperial palace. She plans to keep her head down, but she can't resist solving the mysterious illnesses around her. Soon she catches the eye of Jinshi, the beautiful palace official. It's a clever, charming mystery for fans of court intrigue.
218: How Do We Relationship? by Tamifull (Viz Media) is a yuri romance about real-life relationships. Saeko and Miwa are college freshmen who meet and quickly realize they're both into girls. They start dating, but neither has any idea how to make a relationship work. It's honest, funny, and sometimes messy, for readers who want a realistic love story.
219: Pokémon Adventures: Ruby and Sapphire by Hidenori Kusaka and Satoshi Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a Pokémon adventure series. Ruby loves stylish Pokémon contests, while Sapphire is a wild girl who wants to be a battler. They make a bet to see who can reach their goals in eighty days. Their journey across the Hoenn region gets them caught up in a much bigger fight.
220: The World's Greatest First Love: The Case of Ritsu Onodera by Shungiku Nakamura (Sublime) is a BL romance about life in publishing. Ritsu Onodera quits his father's company to prove himself, only to land as an editor in a shojo manga department. His boss is Masamune Takano, who turns out to be his first love from high school. It's funny, sweet, and full of manga industry drama.
221: Magical Girl Spec-Ops Asuka by Makoto Fukami and Seigo Tokiya (Seven Seas) is a dark action series. Asuka Otori was one of five magical girls who saved the world from an invading army. Now she just wants a normal life in high school, but terrorists are using magic for their own purposes. Asuka must face her past to fight back. It's violent and intense, for fans of darker magical girl stories.
222: No Game No Life by Yuu Kamiya (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel. Sora and Shiro are a brother and sister who are unbeatable at games, but they're shut-ins in real life. Then they're summoned to Disboard, a world where everything is decided by games. Now they set out to conquer it. It's colorful, clever, and full of mind games for fans of strategy.
224: The Sacred Blacksmith by Isao Miura (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action series. Cecily Cambell is a young knight who wants to protect her city, but she's still learning to fight. When she meets Luke, a quiet blacksmith who forges extraordinary swords, she asks him to make one for her. It's a fun fantasy adventure for readers who like knights, magic, and swords with secrets.
225: Cross-Dressing Villainess Cecilia Sylvie by Hiroro Akizakura and Shino Akiyama (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance. Cecilia remembers her past life and realizes she's the villainess in an otome game, doomed to die. To avoid her fate, she disguises herself as a boy named Cecil. Her plan goes well until the game's heroes take an interest in her. It's a fun villainess story full of mix-ups.
229: Queen's Quality by Kyousuke Motomi (Viz Media) is a supernatural romance. Fumi Hosokawa is a Sweeper, someone who can clean people's minds of dark forces, working with her partner Kyutaro. As her powers grow, she learns that she may be destined to become the Queen, an incredibly powerful being. It's a sweet, action-packed story that continues QQ Sweeper.
230: Sasaki and Miyano by Shou Harusono (Yen Press) is a sweet BL romance. Miyano is a high school boy who loves reading BL manga but isn't sure about real romance himself. When a senior, Sasaki, becomes curious about Miyano's books, the two start spending time together. Slowly, their friendship turns into something more. It's gentle, funny, and charming, for readers who like slow-burn romance.
231: High School Debut by Kazune Kawahara (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy. Haruna Nagashima spent middle school playing softball, and now she wants a boyfriend. With no idea where to start, she asks Yoh, a cool and popular senior, to coach her in love, as long as she doesn't fall for him. It's funny, sweet, and full of heart, for fans of classic shojo romance.
233: A Certain Scientific Railgun by Kazuma Kamachi and Motoi Fuyukawa (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi action series. In Academy City, students develop psychic powers. Mikoto Misaka is one of the strongest, a girl who can control electricity. With her friends in Judgment, she fights crime and stumbles into the city's dark secrets. It's fun and action-packed for fans of A Certain Magical Index.
238: Dragonar Academy by Shiki Mizuchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action series. Ash Blake is a student at Ansarivan, a school for dragon riders, but his dragon partner never seems to show up. When he finally gets one, it turns out to be a girl named Eco. Now he must protect her as they figure out their bond. It's a fantasy comedy with ecchi moments and big dragon battles.
242: Happy Mania by Moyoco Anno (Tokyopop) is a josei comedy about the search for love. Kayoko Shigeta is a 24-year-old who wants to find true love, but her relationships always go wrong. She dives from one bad choice to the next, always believing this time will be different. It's honest, chaotic, and funny, for readers who like messy heroines and real-life romance.
244: Welcome to the Ballroom by Tomo Takeuchi (Kodansha) is a sports drama about finding the thing you were meant to do. Tatara Fujita is a timid middle schooler with no hobbies and no plans for his future. When a professional dancer named Kaname Sengoku rescues him from a pair of bullies, Tatara stumbles into a ballroom dance studio and discovers competitive dancing. It's a great pick for readers who love underdog stories, hard work, and dazzling, full-motion art.
245: Bungo Stray Dogs by Kafka Asagiri and Sango Harukawa (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series with a literary twist. Atsushi Nakajima has been thrown out of his orphanage and is starving when he pulls an odd young man named Osamu Dazai out of a river. Dazai turns out to work for the Armed Detective Agency, a group of people with special powers, and Atsushi is pulled into their cases. Readers who like stylish fights, quirky casts, and characters named after famous authors will have fun here.
246: Haganai: I Don't Have Many Friends by Yomi Hirasaka (Seven Seas) is a comedy about lonely teens trying, badly, to fit in. Transfer student Kodaka Hasegawa looks like a delinquent, so nobody will talk to him. Then he meets Yozora Mikazuki, a sharp-tongued girl who has also never made a friend, and she starts a club whose whole purpose is to practice making some. It's an awkward, funny read for fans of harem comedies and misfit casts.
248: Fire Punch by Tatsuki Fujimoto (Viz Media) is a dark, unpredictable action drama from the creator of Chainsaw Man. In a frozen world, some people are born with special blessings, and young Agni's is that he can regenerate from almost any wound. When his village is burned with flames that never go out, Agni survives, burning endlessly, and sets out for revenge. It's intense and strange, best for older readers who like bold, boundary-pushing stories.
249: Land of the Blindfolded by Sakura Tsukuba (CMX) is a gentle shojo romance with a touch of the supernatural. High schooler Kanade Kokura has a secret gift: when she touches people, she can sometimes see glimpses of their future. Then she meets Arou Sakuma, a transfer student who can see people's pasts. Their abilities draw them together as they try to help the people around them. It's a sweet, thoughtful read for fans of quiet romance.
252: UQ Holder by Ken Akamatsu (Kodansha) is a shonen action fantasy set in the same world as Negima! Magister Negi Magi. Touta Konoe is a country boy who dreams of leaving his small village for the big city and the giant space elevator that towers above it. After a brush with death leaves him immortal, he joins UQ Holder, a secret society of people who cannot die. It's a fun, fast read for fans of tournament battles and big casts.
253: Bizenghast by M. Alice LeGrow (Tokyopop) is a gothic fantasy with a spooky, fairy-tale feel. Dinah is an orphan who lives with her aunt in the gloomy town of Bizenghast, where she sees ghosts that no one else can. When she and her friend Vincent stumble on an old mausoleum, Dinah becomes bound to free the restless spirits trapped inside, one night at a time. Readers who enjoy ornate art and eerie puzzles will feel right at home.
254: Citrus+ by Saburouta (Seven Seas) is a yuri romance that continues the story of Citrus. It follows stepsisters Yuzu Aihara, a bubbly, fashionable girl, and Mei Aihara, the serious student council president, as their relationship keeps growing. The series spends more time on the everyday ups and downs of being together, with plenty of familiar faces along the way. It's a natural next step for anyone who finished the original series and wanted more.
256: Tokyo Ghoul:re by Sui Ishida (Viz Media) is a dark horror action series and the sequel to Tokyo Ghoul. Haise Sasaki is an investigator for the CCG, the agency that hunts ghouls, the flesh-eating creatures hiding among humans. Haise is half-ghoul himself, and he leads the Quinx Squad, young investigators who have been given ghoul powers. It's a moody, intense read for fans of the original who want to see where the story goes next.
257: B.O.D.Y. by Ao Mimori (Viz Media) is a shojo romance drama about a crush that turns out to be complicated. High schooler Ryoko has quietly liked her popular, aloof classmate Ryunosuke for a long time. Then she learns his big secret: after school, he works as a paid host for older women. As the two get closer, Ryoko has to decide what she really wants. It's a good fit for readers who like romance with some grown-up drama.
258: Eureka Seven by Jinsei Kataoka and Kazuma Kondou, based on the anime from studio Bones (Bandai), is a sci-fi mecha adventure. Fourteen-year-old Renton Thurston is bored with his small-town life and dreams of joining Gekkostate, a band of rebel sky-surfing pilots. His wish comes true when a giant robot named Nirvash crashes into his grandfather's garage, piloted by a mysterious girl named Eureka. It's a fun read for fans of mecha and coming-of-age stories.
259: My Instant Death Ability Is So Overpowered by Tsuyoshi Fujitaka (J-Novel Club) is a dark fantasy comedy that pokes fun at isekai stories. When Yogiri Takatou's whole class is summoned to another world, everyone gets special powers except Yogiri, who slept through the whole thing. Left behind as useless, he turns out to have an ability nobody expected: he can kill anything just by wishing it dead. It's for readers who like an unbeatable hero and a sly sense of humor.
261: Tista by Tatsuya Endo (Viz Media) is a short, moody action drama from the creator of Spy x Family. In New York City, a quiet young woman named Tista Long works as a skilled assassin, targeting people the church has judged to be sinners. Her lonely, carefully controlled life begins to change when she crosses paths with a young artist. It's a quick, bittersweet read for fans of Endo's work who want to see where his style began.
262: Tramps Like Us by Yayoi Ogawa (Tokyopop) is a josei romantic comedy about an unusual living arrangement. Sumire Iwaya is a successful journalist whose career is going well and whose love life is not. One night she finds a handsome young man in a cardboard box outside her apartment and takes him in, naming him Momo after her childhood dog, on the condition that he acts as her pet. It's a funny, warm read for adults who like their romance offbeat.
263: Noragami: Stray God by Adachitoka (Kodansha) is a supernatural action series with plenty of heart and humor. Yato is a minor god with no shrine and no worshippers, so he takes odd jobs for five yen apiece, hoping to build a following. When high schooler Hiyori Iki saves him from a bus, she ends up with her soul slipping out of her body, and she needs Yato's help to fix it. It's a great pick for fans of spirits, sword fights, and found family.
266: You Like Me, Not My Daughter?! by Kota Nozomi (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy with a twist. Ayako Katsuragi has raised her niece Miu as her own daughter for ten years, and she's sure their college-aged neighbor Takumi has a crush on Miu. Instead, Takumi confesses that it's Ayako he's in love with. Flustered and doubtful, she has to figure out how she really feels. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of older-heroine romance.
267: Play It Cool, Guys by Kokone Nata (Yen Press) is a lighthearted comedy about looking cool and failing at it. Four handsome young men seem effortlessly composed to everyone who sees them on the street. In reality, each one is a lovable mess, tripping over small mistakes and awkward moments while trying very hard to keep his cool. Its short, gentle chapters make it a great pick for readers who want a cheerful, low-stakes laugh.
268: Skull-face Bookseller Honda-san by Honda (Yen Press) is a workplace comedy drawn from the creator's real life in a bookstore. Honda works at a busy shop in Japan, where he wears a skull mask and handles a stream of unusual customer requests, from foreign visitors to hard-to-find titles. It's a funny, affectionate look at the book business and the people who keep it running. Book lovers and anyone who has worked retail will see themselves here.
271: Yu-Gi-Oh! R by Akira Ito, from the original series by Kazuki Takahashi (Viz Media), is a shonen action side story about high-stakes card games. Yako Tenma, the adopted heir of Duel Monsters creator Maximillion Pegasus, blames Yugi Muto for his mentor's downfall. He seizes the KaibaCorp tower and challenges Yugi to a series of duels to settle the score. It's a fun bonus for fans who grew up on the original manga and anime.
272: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya by Nagaru Tanigawa and Gaku Tsugano (Yen Press) is a sci-fi comedy based on the hit light novels. Kyon is an ordinary high schooler until he ends up seated in front of Haruhi Suzumiya, who announces on day one that she only cares about aliens, time travelers, and espers. Before long she drags him into her new club, the SOS Brigade, to hunt for the strange. It's a playful, clever read for fans of quirky school comedies.
274: Uncle from Another World by Hotondoshindeiru (Yen Press) is a comedy that flips the usual isekai story on its head. College student Takafumi picks up his uncle from the hospital after he wakes from a seventeen-year coma. It turns out his uncle spent all that time in a fantasy world, and he came back with real magic and no idea what's happened to video games since. It's a funny, nostalgic read for longtime gamers and fantasy fans.
275: A Man and His Cat by Umi Sakurai (Square Enix) is a gentle, heartwarming slice-of-life story. Fukumaru is a chubby, unusual-looking cat who has been sitting in a pet store for a long time, sure that nobody will ever want him. Then a quiet, middle-aged widower named Fuyuki Kanda walks in and chooses him. The two lonely souls slowly learn to be a family. It's perfect for cat lovers and anyone who needs a cozy, feel-good read.
276: Whisper Me a Love Song by Eku Takeshima (Kodansha) is a sweet yuri romance about music and first love. On her first day of high school, Himari Kino hears upperclassman Yori Asanagi sing with her band and is completely blown away. When Himari tells Yori she loves her, she means it as a fan, but Yori takes it as a real confession and falls for her. It's a tender, charming read for fans of school romance and music stories.
277: Red River by Chie Shinohara (Viz Media) is a sweeping shojo historical fantasy and romance. Yuri Suzuki is an ordinary fifteen-year-old in Tokyo until a pair of ghostly hands pulls her into a puddle and out into the ancient Hittite Empire. A scheming queen wants to use her as a human sacrifice, and Yuri's only protector is the handsome Prince Kail. It's an adventurous, romantic read for anyone who loves palace intrigue and time-slip stories.
278: I Think Our Son Is Gay by Okura (Square Enix) is a warm family comedy. Tomoko Aoyama is a cheerful homemaker who is pretty sure her teenage son Hiroki is gay, since he keeps almost saying so before catching himself. Rather than push him, she quietly decides to support him and wait until he's ready to tell her. Its short chapters are kind, funny, and full of love, making it a great pick for anyone who wants a feel-good family story.
279: Blue Spring Ride (Ao Haru Ride) by Io Sakisaka (Viz Media) is a shojo romance drama about second chances. In middle school, Futaba Yoshioka had a crush on a gentle boy named Kou Tanaka, but he moved away before anything could happen. Now in high school, Futaba is trying to reinvent herself when Kou reappears with a new last name and a much colder attitude. It's a heartfelt read for fans of slow-burn school romance and friendship.
283: Hinamatsuri by Masao Ohtake (One Peace Books) is an offbeat sci-fi comedy. Yoshifumi Nitta is an up-and-coming yakuza with a nice apartment and a love of fancy vases. His life is turned upside down when a strange capsule lands in his living room and out pops Hina, an expressionless girl with powerful psychic abilities. Before he knows it, he's raising her. It's a hilarious, surprisingly sweet read for fans of deadpan humor and found family.
284: Non Non Biyori by Atto (Seven Seas) is a gentle slice-of-life comedy set in the Japanese countryside. Hotaru Ichijo moves from Tokyo to a tiny rural village whose school has only five students, all in different grades. There she befriends Renge Miyauchi and the other local kids as they fill their days with simple adventures, from catching bugs to exploring the fields. It's a calm, cozy read for anyone who wants a slower, kinder pace.
285: The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn't a Guy at All by Sumiko Arai (Yen Press) is a sweet yuri romance about music and identity. High schooler Aya has a crush on the cool, quiet clerk at her favorite record shop. What she doesn't know is that the clerk is actually Mitsuki, a girl from her own school who loves rock music. As the two bond over their favorite bands, feelings start to grow. It's a charming, funny read for fans of gentle romance.
288: Crimson Spell by Ayano Yamane (Sublime) is a mature fantasy boys' love story. Prince Vald draws a legendary sword from his family's treasury and is cursed by it, turning into a fearsome demon at night. He seeks help from Halvir, a powerful and mysterious sorcerer, who agrees to travel with him in search of a cure. Their journey is full of magic and growing attraction. It's for adult readers who enjoy fantasy adventure with steamy romance.
289: Gunslinger Girl by Yu Aida (ADV) is a quiet, heavy seinen action drama. In modern Italy, a secret government agency takes in young girls who are dying or badly injured and rebuilds them with cybernetic bodies. Conditioned to be loyal, they are trained as assassins and paired with adult handlers. The story focuses on the bonds between the girls and their handlers. It's a thoughtful, melancholy read for older fans of political thrillers.
290: Black Cat by Kentaro Yabuki (Viz Media) is a shonen action series with a cool, laid-back hero. Train Heartnet was once Black Cat, the deadliest assassin of the secret organization Chronos.
