Now he has left that life behind and works as a sweeper, a bounty hunter, alongside his partner Sven, chasing criminals and usually missing out on the reward money. It's a fun, stylish read for fans of gunfights, sharp banter, and early-2000s action.
291: Girl Got Game by Shizuru Seino is a shojo romantic comedy with a sporty twist. Kyo Aizawa's basketball-obsessed father enrolls her at a high school as a boy so she can play on the boys' team and live out his dreams. Worse, she ends up rooming with Chiharu, the team's grumpy star player. Keeping her secret gets harder by the day. It's a fun, breezy read for fans of gender-swap comedies and sports romance.
292: Kiss Him, Not Me! by Junko (Kodansha) is a shojo comedy that turns the dating game upside down. Kae Serinuma is a devoted fan girl who loves imagining the boys at school as couples. When her favorite anime character dies, she's so heartbroken that she loses a lot of weight in a week, and suddenly four boys want to date her. All Kae wants is for them to date each other. It's a laugh-out-loud read for anyone who's loved a fandom.
293: Nodame Cantabile by Tomoko Ninomiya is a josei comedy and romance set in the world of classical music. Shinichi Chiaki is a gifted, perfectionist music student who dreams of conducting in Europe but is stuck in Japan by his fear of flying. Then he meets his neighbor, Megumi "Nodame" Noda, a messy, eccentric pianist with remarkable talent. It's a funny, warm read for music lovers and fans of oddball couples.
294: Black Torch by Tsuyoshi Takaki (Viz Media) is a shonen action series with ninjas and spirits. Jiro Azuma comes from a long line of ninja and has a rare gift: he can talk to animals. When he rescues a wounded black cat, it turns out to be Rago, a legendary mononoke, and saving it pulls Jiro into a hidden war between humans and spirits. It's a fast, punchy read for fans of supernatural battles and cool creature designs.
295: The Hero Laughs While Walking the Path of Vengeance a Second Time by Nero Kizuka (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy light novel about revenge. Kaito was summoned to another world as a hero, only to be betrayed and killed by the very people he fought to save. Somehow, he wakes up back at the start of his journey with all his memories intact, and this time he plans to make them pay. It's a grim read for adults who like antiheroes and revenge stories.
296: Blank Canvas: My So-Called Artist's Journey by Akiko Higashimura (Seven Seas) is a funny and moving memoir in manga form. As a high schooler, Akiko is sure she's destined to become a famous manga artist. Hoping to get into art school, she joins a painting class run by Mr. Hidaka, a tough, sword-swinging teacher who pushes her harder than anyone ever has. It's a heartfelt read for artists, dreamers, and anyone who's had a teacher who changed their life.
298: Angels of Death by Kudan Naduka, based on the game by Makoto Sanada (Yen Press), is a horror thriller. Thirteen-year-old Rachel Gardner wakes up in the basement of a strange building with no memory of how she got there. As she tries to escape, she meets Zack, a bandaged killer with a scythe, and the two make an unusual promise: if he helps her get out, he'll kill her when they do. It's a tense, creepy read for horror fans.
300: Yuuna and the Haunted Hot Springs by Tadahiro Miura (Seven Seas) is a supernatural comedy with lots of fan service. Kogarashi Fuyuzora is a broke teen with strong spiritual powers who moves into Yuragi-sou, a former hot springs inn with surprisingly cheap rent. The reason is soon clear: the inn is haunted by Yuuna, a friendly ghost girl with no memory of her past. It's a silly, playful read for older teens and adults who enjoy ecchi comedy.
302: Hellsing by Kouta Hirano (Dark Horse) is a gory, stylish action horror series. The Hellsing Organization protects Britain from vampires and other monsters, and its greatest weapon is Alucard, an ancient and powerful vampire who serves the Hellsing family. When young police officer Seras Victoria is caught in one of his missions, her life takes a dramatic turn. The Deluxe Edition collects the series in big hardcovers, great for fans of over-the-top gothic action.
303: We Were There by Yuki Obata (Viz Media) is a shojo romance drama about first love and loss. Nanami Takahashi starts high school hoping to make friends and soon finds herself drawn to Motoharu Yano, the most popular boy in her class. As they grow closer, Nanami learns that Yano is still carrying grief over the death of his former girlfriend. It's an emotional, realistic read for fans of romance that takes its time.
304: Peach Fuzz by Lindsay Cibos and Jared Hodges (Tokyopop) is a cute, funny story for young readers. Nine-year-old Amanda finally gets the pet she's always wanted, a ferret named Peach. The trouble is that Peach thinks she's a princess and Amanda is a monster, so the two get off to a rocky start. Told from both of their points of view, it's a sweet, silly read for kids and families who love animals.
305: Mixed Vegetables by Ayumi Komura (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy about food and family. Hanayu Ashitaba is the daughter of a pastry shop owner, but she secretly dreams of becoming a sushi chef. Hayato Hyuga is the heir to a famous sushi restaurant, and he wants to be a pastry chef. When the two meet at a culinary high school, sparks fly. It's a sweet, tasty read for fans of cooking stories and light romance.
306: Hell's Paradise: Jigokuraku by Yuji Kaku (Viz Media) is a shonen action horror series. Gabimaru the Hollow is a legendary ninja on death row who no execution can kill. He is offered a pardon if he can find the elixir of life on a mysterious island that no one has ever returned from. Joined by Sagiri, the executioner assigned to watch him, he sets out. It's a strange, beautiful, and violent read for fans of dark battle manga.
308: Hot Gimmick by Miki Aihara (Viz Media) is a shojo romance drama set in a gossipy company housing complex. Hatsumi Narita quietly buys a pregnancy test for her younger sister, but bossy neighbor Ryoki Tachibana finds out. He threatens to tell everyone unless Hatsumi does whatever he says. Things get even more tangled when her childhood friend Azusa moves back into the complex. It's a dramatic, soapy read for older teens who like messy love triangles.
309: Ninja vs. Gokudo by Shinsuke Kondo (Kodansha) is a shonen action thriller about two sides at war. Shinoha is a young man who has never been able to smile, until he meets Kiwami, a kind, gentle man who makes him laugh. The problem is that Shinoha is secretly a shinobi, and Kiwami is a yakuza, members of two groups that have hated each other for centuries. It's a stylish, violent read for fans of dark action and odd-couple bonds.
311: Tower Dungeon by Tsutomu Nihei (Kodansha) is a seinen dark fantasy from the creator of Blame! and Knights of Sidonia. When a powerful sorcerer kidnaps the princess and takes her to the top of a vast tower, the kingdom sends soldiers to rescue her. Yuva, a young and inexperienced recruit, joins the mission and begins the dangerous climb through the tower's monster-filled floors. It's a moody, atmospheric read for fans of dungeon crawls and striking architecture.
312: Flying Witch by Chihiro Ishizuka (Vertical) is a gentle slice-of-life fantasy. Makoto Kowata is a fifteen-year-old witch-in-training who moves from Yokohama to the countryside of Aomori to live with her relatives, along with her black cat, Chito. Her magic is woven into ordinary days of gardening, school, and exploring the town, delighting her young cousin Chinatsu. It's a calm, cozy read for anyone who likes small wonders and quiet country life.
313: Wandering Witch: The Journey of Elaina by Jougi Shiraishi and Itsuki Nanao (Square Enix) is a fantasy adventure based on the popular light novels. Elaina is a young witch who has finally earned her title. Inspired by the books she loved as a child, she sets off alone on her broom to travel the world, visiting one strange country after another. Each stop brings a new story, some sweet and some bittersweet. It's a lovely read for fans of travel tales.
316: Karakuri Odette by Julietta Suzuki (Tokyopop) is a sweet, funny shojo story about what it means to be human. Odette is an android built by the brilliant Professor Yoshizawa. Curious about people, she decides to go to high school, where she struggles to understand feelings, friendships, and her own super-strength. Along the way she meets a delinquent named Asao. It's a gentle read for fans of Suzuki's Kamisama Kiss and heartfelt school comedies.
317: K-On! by Kakifly (Yen Press) is a cheerful slice-of-life comedy about music and friendship. Yui Hirasawa starts high school with no hobbies and no idea what to do with her free time. She signs up for the light music club, which needs one more member to avoid being shut down, even though she's never played an instrument. Before long she's learning guitar and drinking tea with her new bandmates. It's a cozy, upbeat read for fans of gentle comedy.
318: Sweat and Soap by Kintetsu Yamada (Kodansha) is a seinen workplace romance. Asako Yaeyama is an office worker who is very self-conscious about how much she sweats. She works at a company that makes soaps and toiletries, and one day she meets Koutarou Natori, the company's star product developer, who loves the way she smells. It's a sweet, funny, adult romance with kind leads, great for readers who want a feel-good love story.
319: From Eroica with Love by Yasuko Aoike (CMX) is a classic shojo comedy and spy adventure. Dorian Red Gloria, the Earl of Gloria, is a flamboyant English aristocrat who moonlights as Eroica, a gentleman thief with a taste for priceless art. His capers keep colliding with Major Klaus von dem Eberbach, a stern, by-the-book NATO officer who can't stand him. It's a witty, globe-trotting read for fans of Cold War spy stories and odd-couple banter.
320: InuYasha by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a shonen action fantasy and romance. On her fifteenth birthday, Kagome Higurashi falls down an old well on her family's shrine and lands in feudal Japan. There she frees InuYasha, a half-demon pinned to a tree, but soon the magical Shikon Jewel is shattered, and the two must work together to find the pieces. It's a timeless adventure for fans of demons, swordplay, and slow-burn romance.
321: Kiniro Mosaic by Yui Hara (Yen Press) is a gentle slice-of-life comedy about friendship across cultures. While on a homestay in England, Japanese student Shinobu Omiya befriends Alice Cartelet, the daughter of her host family. Years later, Alice arrives in Japan to attend Shinobu's high school, joined by a growing circle of friends. It's a sweet, lighthearted read for anyone who enjoys cute school days and warm everyday humor.
